metadata.title: minimal-uniformity-three: machine-checked companion to "Minimal uniformity three: unit-edge tilings around the non-Archimedean vertex types"
metadata.description: The verification artifact for the paper's claims: the U(z) minimal-uniformity ladder (the k = 1 scan, the k <= 2 catalogue and refutation, the four rigid uniformity-3 witnesses, the essential-irregularity verdicts), re-derived in exact rational and cyclotomic arithmetic, and the k <= 2 DRAT completeness certificate — 24 UNSAT obligations over the tier-1 certification universe, kissat-solved and drat-trim-verified. The repository holds only the claim specs; all machinery is the pinned research-core library.
metadata.notes: If you cite this verification artifact, please cite the specific archived version you checked, not the repository in general. Each release has its own version DOI; see the "Archival" section in README.md.

metadata.title: The network that learned to run itself
metadata.description: The limitations of traditional automation with scale and complexity have given rise to a powerful new concept - hyper-automation - Mostly for IT and cybersecurity areas. It is a system that allows machines to be self-managed and self-adaptive through AI, machine learning, and software orchestration, reducing human intervention. Streaming services, IoT sensors, and remote works are just some of the main drivers that bring about the need to shift traditional rule-based automation to proactive, self-regulating networks, which are enabled by real-time monitoring and decision-making like, for example, congestion prevention and resource allocation done autonomously by AIOps tools. So, 24x7 security, with minimum downtime and human error, is possible to achieve by organizations. Meanwhile, the reliance on autonomous systems creates important questions about trust responsibility accountability and Because of this, the necessity of effective oversight as well as the presence of highly trained personnel who are capable of handling these technologies will become paramount to the equation. Businesses that implement hyper-automation [1] well may end up far ahead of the competitors that still rely on manual processes. It just goes to show that as the network landscape evolves, the organizations that are going to thrive are the ones adopting hyper-automation at a deep level. In the end, getting on board with hyper-automation is not only a futuristic consideration, it is a requirement for organizations who desire to be competitive in the digital world.[14][15][16][17]

metadata.title: Axiomatic Constraint Compilation and Discrete Mechanics A Linear Synthesis of Scalar Algebras, Action Emergence, and State-Space Addressability
metadata.description:
Axiomatic Constraint Compilation and Discrete Mechanics

A Linear Synthesis of Scalar Algebras, Action Emergence, and State-Space Addressability

Driven by Dean Kulik

July 2026

 

 

Scientific models have historically operated on substance-based ontologies, treating matter, space, and time as foundational entities governed by external physical laws. An alternative paradigm—the constraint-compilation framework—reconstructs physical and computational reality from an axiomatic foundation based on the operational limits of state transitions. By establishing a small set of primitive constraints governing system updates, higher-order physical structures—including local conservation laws, the complex scalar field, Hamilton's principle, gauge symmetries, and discrete permutation mechanics—are derived directly as mathematical necessities.

The core mechanism across all these domains is addressability in change: a constrained system expands its effective capability not by violating its underlying rules, but by discovering new representation spaces and orthogonal channels that exploit latent structural addressability. This report provides a linear synthesis of the complete theoretical framework and empirical corpus. It details the axiomatic pipeline, extracts all compiled theorems and novel quantitative measurements, and outlines the structural audit trail governing the framework's internal consistency.

Primitive Constraint Architecture and Topological State Space

The framework begins with five irreducible primitive constraints that define the admissibility of state space configurations. These constraints do not act as external rules applied to pre-existing objects; rather, they define the topological boundaries outside of which no physical or computational state can exist.

Constraint 0 establishes that distinction exists (). It defines the undifferentiated ground state, where total global connection behaves locally as a void. Graph-theoretically, Constraint 0 is represented by a complete graph  whose Laplacian matrix  yields a spectrum of vibrational modes consisting of a single zero eigenvalue with multiplicity 1 (representing global monolithic translation) and an excited eigenvalue  with multiplicity  (representing maximal connectivity and stiffness). Traversing a boundary walk on a 12-cell cylindrical manifold yields a stasis period of 12 steps across a single face, whereas introducing an offset seam transforms the topology into a Möbius strip with a face-parity twist, forcing a 24-step traversal that serializes superposition into temporal sequence.

Constraint 1 mandates continuation: every admissible state  must admit at least one legal successor  () under the transition algebra. Terminal states and static fixed points are strictly excluded. Topologically, Constraint 1 mandates a nowhere-vanishing vector field on the compact state manifold . By the Poincaré-Hopf theorem, the sum of the indices of the vector field's zeros equals the Euler characteristic ; because zeros are forbidden, the manifold must satisfy .

Constraint 1a establishes independence preservation: independent distinctions remain independently continuable. For independent continuation operators  and , joint evolution must factor as , enforcing the algebraic commutation condition . This single commutator serves as a structural spine operating across three distinct layers: at the transition algebra layer it eliminates coordination channels to enforce local conservation; at the scalar algebra layer it forces commutativity to select the complex numbers; and at the symmetry layer it constrains gauge sector factorization.

Constraint 2 enforces history preservation: every continuation preserves the set of states reachable from prior history, forbidding the deletion of accessible nodes from the transition graph. Iterated transition functions over finite sets yield descending chains  which inevitably terminate at a fixed point . To prevent the flow of possibility from freezing, Constraint 2 forces the physical state space to possess infinite degrees of freedom.

Constraint 5 defines the observable event primitive: an observable event is the minimal continuation simultaneously carrying two independent degrees of freedom, continuous spatial propagation and a distinct temporal residue. Constraint 5 forces the real dimension of the scalar continuation algebra to satisfy , while spontaneous symmetry breaking eliminates the static vacuum as a forbidden fixed point.

Rigorously auditing the primitive set demonstrates that initial formulations contained redundant axioms. At the binary base (), Constraint 1 alone forces the unique legal state transition map to be bijective (the swap map), rendering Constraint 2 derivable rather than primitive at the foundational layer. Similarly, uniform in-degree and isotropic change are derived directly from Constraint 1 when combined with a discrete difference operator.

The Division Algebra Theorem and Complex Continuation Amplitudes

Standard quantum field theory postulates complex-valued probability amplitudes. The Division Algebra Theorem replaces axiomatic postulation with a proof demonstrating that the complex field  is the unique admissible scalar continuation algebra under the primitive constraint set .

metadata.title: Misapplication of statistics in scorpiology: a case study
metadata.description: A recent paper by Ait Hammou et al. (2026) studied morphometric differentiation among Androctonus aeneas C. L. Koch, 1839, A. liouvillei (Pallary, 1924), and putative hybrids from Algeria, based on 23 linear measurements from 12 females. The present article re-examines the statistical procedures applied therein through an independent reproduction of all reported analyses using the same data matrix. Six categories of issues are identified. (1) The 23 variables consist exclusively of raw absolute-size measurements and thus contain no shape information. The first principal component, which accounts for 71.6 % of the total variance, shows uniformly negative loadings across all 23 variables and thus represents a generalized size axis. (2) Two data anomalies (the carapace length of A. aeneas (Rechaiga) and the telson width of A. liouvillei (Arbouat bayadh) are statistically incompatible with the remainder of the dataset. The true carapace length of A. aeneas (Rechaiga) is reconstructed as 26.97 mm using two independent geometric methods. (3) The sample size (n = 12, distributed 7 : 3 : 2) invalidates the authors’ multivariate procedures in several mathematically distinct ways: degenerate within-group variance for A. aeneas, unreliable asymptotic approximation in the Kruskal-Wallis test, and a singular within-class scatter matrix preventing linear discriminant analysis from running under a standard implementation (R’s MASS::lda() returns the error “variables are collinear”). (4) No correction for multiple comparisons was applied to the 23 simultaneous univariate tests. None of the three variables reported as “significant” by the authors remains significant after either Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg correction, even when exact rather than asymptotic p-values are used. (5) The authors’ verbal interpretations of their PCA, HCA, and LDA results contradict the corresponding figures, while PCA and HCA partition the 12 specimens in qualitatively different ways. (6) Re-analysis after Mosimann log-shape ratio transformation, which removes the dominant size component, places the three putative hybrids within the A. liouvillei point cloud rather than between the two parental species. In a DAPC of the size-corrected data with regularized dimensionality (n.pca = 2), the training-set classification accuracy decreases from 100% (the value implicitly obtained by the authors’ p > N−g LDA) to 67%. The hybrid status of the three specimens assigned a priori on the basis of collection from “contact zones” is therefore unsupported by any multivariate analysis once size is properly disentangled from shape.

metadata.title: Design, Synthesis, Characterization And In Vitro Antileishmanial Evaluation Of 2,4,6-Substituted Pyrimidine Derivatives Conjugated With Imidazole Moieties
metadata.description: The present study describes the design, synthesis, preliminary characterization, and in vitro antileishmanial evaluation of a focused series of imidazole-conjugated 2,4,6-substituted pyrimidine derivatives designated UG-1 to UG-10. The compounds were designed through scaffold hybridization involving a substituted imidazole moiety, a para-phenylene linker, and a 2-aminopyrimidine core bearing electronically diverse aryl substituents. The synthetic route comprised three sequential stages: nucleophilic aromatic substitution of 2-substituted imidazoles with 4-fluorobenzaldehyde in dry N,N-dimethylformamide using potassium carbonate and hexadecyltrimethylammonium bromide; Claisen–Schmidt condensation of the resulting aldehyde intermediates with substituted acetophenones; and cyclocondensation of the chalcone intermediates with guanidine hydrochloride in ethanolic sodium hydroxide. The target derivatives were obtained in yields ranging from 55% to 85%. Thin-layer chromatography produced Rf values between 0.130 and 0.80, indicating differences in chromatographic behaviour across the compound series. FT-IR analysis provided functional-group-level evidence for the presence of amino, aromatic, imine, cyano, nitro, methoxy, and chloro functionalities in the relevant derivatives. Biological evaluation identified UG-9, an ethyl-imidazole derivative containing a 3-chlorophenyl substituent, as the most promising compound in the supplied dataset. UG-9 exhibited IC₅₀ values of 11.2 µM against Leishmania promastigotes and 8.6 µM against intracellular amastigotes. Cytotoxicity evaluation against RAW 264.7 macrophages produced a CC₅₀ value of 126.4 µM, corresponding to an intracellular amastigote-based selectivity index of 14.7. These findings indicate that imidazole-conjugated 2-amino-4,6-diarylpyrimidines represent a potentially useful early-stage chemotype for antileishmanial optimization. Nevertheless, independent replicate experiments, complete activity profiling of the compound series, comparison with standard antileishmanial drugs, expanded cytotoxicity studies, and mechanistic validation are required before definitive lead selection can be established.

metadata.title: New insights into estimating the cementation exponent of the tight and deep carbonate pore systems via rigorous numerical strategies
metadata.description: One of the main constituents of any reservoir characterization is an accurate forecast of water saturation, which is highly dependent upon the cementation exponent. Even though there have been a lot of studies, the most common correlations depend on total porosity. This means that they do not work as well in heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs, especially tight formations with total porosities less than 10%. This study aims to develop accurate and universal models for estimating the cementation exponent in deep and tight carbonate pore systems located in West Asia. Two heuristic algorithms, including the radial basis function neural network optimized by ant colony optimization (RBFNN-ACO) and gene expression programming (GEP), were employed to calculate the cementation exponent. To do this, we prepared a databank incorporating cementation exponents, total porosity, and various pore types. Then, the databank is classified into the test subset (for model prediction checking) and the train subset (for model construction). The reliability of the new recommended models is inspected by applying several statistical quality measures associated with graphical analyses. So, the consequences of the modeling disclose the large precision of the above-mentioned RBFNN-ACO, GEP Model-I, and GEP Model-II by average absolute percentage relative deviations (AAPRD%) of 6.28%, 6.39%, and 7.45%, respectively. Based on the outliers analysis, nearly 95% of the databank and model estimations are, respectively, valid and reliable. Additionally, the three input variables, including moldic porosity (with a + 70% impact value), non-fabric-selective dissolution (connected) porosity (with a -30% impact value), and interparticle porosity (with a -23% impact value), exhibit the main affecting parameters on the cementation exponent. Comparing current results with traditional literature correlations demonstrates the supremacy of the RBFNN-ACO model (AAPRD = 6.28% and root mean squared error (RMSE) = 0.17) over the examined literature correlations such as Borai’s equation (AAPRD = 12.30% and RMSE = 0.41). In addition, RBFNN-ACO can give better results than Borai’s Eqn. for tight (porosity less than 10%) and deep carbonate samples.

metadata.description: Anonymised responses from 45 STEM researchers across Algerian universities (Google Forms, April–May 2026, administered in Arabic). Contains categorical background items (Part A), 31 Likert items across five sections (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree; several items positively worded and reverse-scored in analysis), one multi-select reviewer-commentary item, and three open-ended items. Timestamps and the consent-confirmation column removed; respondents identified only as R01–R45. Supports the article "Challenges of Algerian STEM Researchers in English-Medium Scholarly Publishing" (Chergui & Boudinar). A README sheet documents the variables.

metadata.title: Promoting inclusive rural development: A mixed-methods evaluation of TEKAD's impact in eastern Indonesia
metadata.description:
Persistent rural disparities in Indonesia’s eastern provinces necessitate innovative, inclusive development approaches.

The Transformasi Ekonomi Kampung Terpadu (TEKAD) program, a partnership between the Indonesian

government and the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), aims to transform rural

economies through participatory planning, micro-enterprise support, and enhanced financial and institutional

access. This study employs a sequential mixed-methods approach, analysing quantitative data from 698

households across 47 villages in ten regencies at Eastern Indonesia namely, Papua Island, Nusa Tenggara Timur

and Maluku, complemented by qualitative insights from interviews and observations. This research found that

the program’s outcomes exceed the targets for financial access and market access but underperformed in productivity,

technology adoption, institutional trust, and investment satisfaction, particularly in fisheries and regions

with weak governance. People with disabilities faced significant exclusion, highlighting deficiencies in

TEKAD’s Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) framework. The study reveals tensions between

decentralized development and implementation consistency, aligning with adaptive governance scholarship.

Recommendations include context-sensitive strategies, universal design principles, and integrated value-

chain planning to enhance equitable rural transformation in Indonesia and similar settings.
